source.title: Shinners & Mahler's Illustrated Flora of North Central Texas
source.authors: Diggs, G. M. Jr.; Lipscomb, B. L.; O'Kennon, R. J.

morphology_documented.habit: Much-branched shrub or small tree (genus); reddish-brown bark (species)
morphology_documented.leaves: Small alternate sessile scales, ovate, acute to acuminate (genus and key)
morphology_documented.flowers: Five-parted pinkish or pale flowers in clustered spicate racemes; obovate petals persistent, staminal filaments inserted beneath disk near margin (key)
morphology_documented.habitat: Sand and silt along rivers, reservoirs and disturbed land; escaped cultivation

source_scope_note: Direct species-level details separated from genus/key information; absent historical treatments not filled by unsupported inference.
unresolved_taxonomy_or_source_notes: Flora warns T. chinensis and T. ramosissima can be difficult to distinguish; possible hybridization
Species introduced from Eurasia; not Hays native
preservation: Additive record only; photos, credits, species records and published site unchanged
